title: 5 AI Agents Every Business Should Have Running  #techtok #businessautomation #agent
description:
Five AI agents that should be running in every business by the end of this year. None of these are optional anymore.

Inbox triage reads every email, categorizes by urgency, drafts replies for the easy ones, and flags the rest. Saves two hours a day.

Lead qualifier pulls company info, scores fit, books a call if it is hot, and sends a nurture sequence if it is not. Replaces your SDR for inbound.
Meeting prep researches the company before every call, summarizes past interactions, and drafts talking points. Walk into every meeting fully briefed.
Weekly reporter pulls metrics from your CRM, ad accounts, and finance tools and writes a one-page summary every Monday. Replaces a status meeting.
Support escalator reads every ticket, resolves the easy ones, and escalates the rest with full context attached. Cuts your support team's workload in half.

Build these one at a time over thirty days. Start with whatever is costing you the most right now.
transcript: Five AI agents that everybody should be running by the end of the year. Honestly, none of these are optional anymore. These five together replace 10 hours of work a week across your team. And some of them even replace entire roles. This is AI agents for businesses part seven. Agent one is inbox triage. This reads every email, categorizes it based off what you specify. So, if it's an important one, it'll put into the important piece. Less important, it'll move down the line. What it does is that it makes sure that you read the most important emails first, rather than just spending two hours a day skimming through all the fluff that's unnecessary. Agent two, lead qualifier. This is one that takes your leads automatically, company info, and then decides if it's a good fit or not. It can send different nurture sequences based off of it's a hot lead or a warm one, and replaces or assists your SDR for inbound. Agent three is meeting prep. Before every single call, this agent will do research about the person you're about to talk to, find information about their business, and draft out a plan for how you can come to that call prepared. Agent four, weekly reporter. This goes through all of your stuff, meaning your Gmail, your project management system, CRM, if you're spending ads. It will gather all the information from wherever you store your data, and then give you a weekly report summarizing all the good things you did, but also all the bad things. That way you can have action items at the end of the week to improve the next one. And agent five is support escalator. This is where clients in your communication channels, or for example, people on your app are able to send out tickets whenever there are problems with fulfillment. This AI agent will go through each of those tickets and organize them similar to the email triage, but organize them based off priority. Build these one at a time over the next 30 days. But there's no good order. Just start with the one where the pain hurts the most. Part eight is a warning. I'm going to be talking about the three biggest mistakes that tend to show up whenever building out any of these AI agents. Follow for more.
